So, about four months ago, my school had organized a special day where everyone in the school could dress up as any character from a book, real or fictional. This event had been a yearly thing since 2011, and I was that one person who never went as an actual book character. I would go as either a video game, TV show/movie character or some stupid meme that's irrelevant right now.

A few weeks prior to the event occurring, one of my friends suggested I should go as Dylan Klebold(one of the Columbine shooters) for the parade. At first, I thought he was joking, so I laughed it off and told him "Good idea". But then he said something along the lines of, "You should actually go as him, see if anyone notices."

I kinda felt strange after hearing that, since that one sentence kinda made me debate with myself whether I should actually go as him or not. I'm fourteen, so it's no surprise I would be as stupid as to getting into a conflict with myself about doing something so crazy.

Since, at the time, me and my friends constantly made jokes about school shootings(heck, even our Discord server's theme was changed from Fallout to Columbine For humor purposes), my final decision was that I would go as him.

As far as I know, my friend suggested that I should go as Dylan specifically because I have the exact hair length(but not color) as him and my facial features were faintly reminiscent of him.

'Funny' thing was, when my class took a trip to the library(which I think was one day before me and my friend discussed the dress up), I took a look around for Sue Klebold's(Dylan's mother) book 'A Mother's Reckoning' because since we joked about Columbine a lot and I lacked knowledge of the massacre, I wanted to research it out of curiosity, and for the sake of making insensitive edgy jokes about it. Eventually I found it, borrowed it and began reading it.

Ok, so fast forward to one day prior to the dress up parade, I still had Sue's book in my possession, my teachers passed it off as an interest in a historical event. My mother took me and my older sister for last minute shopping for costumes for the parade. I only needed a black shirt, black cap and faux guns in which I did manage to get.

So I told her I was going as some Sherlock Holmes character(and honestly, I wish I just said I was going as Neo from The Matrix cos that just makes me cringe now) and she passed it off as that, since she only likes hearing small details. And I might as well mention that my sister was aware of the fact that I was going as Dylan, and she let me off the hook from telling my parents who I really was gonna be since she also liked meme related things, and she knew Columbine was a meme, sooo... Yeah. When we arrived home, I immediately assembled my outfit for the next day and wore it to see how it looked on me.

As soon as I saw myself, I laughed and thought of how great of an idea it was. Oh, how deluded I was. Don't think I didn't have second thoughts though. I did, and I was considering going as my favorite singer like I did in 2016.

Finally, the 2017 Book Dress Up Parade arrives, and I also arrive at school, leather trenchcoat flowing behind me. I walked into the high school area(my school, in American terms, combines elementary school with high school), and my friends immediately die of laughter. One of them literally fell to the ground due to laughing so hard. We gathered around, one of my friends saying, "I didn't think you'd actually go as a school shooter, oh my God!".

Me and my friends talked about it for a little bit whilst other classmates and kids from seventh and eighth grade questioned/recognized who I was(in my school there's no eleventh/twelfth grades so high school is just 7/8 and 9/10. I'm in ninth grade since my grade was moved up due to something along the lines of me being born in June or something).

Those who recognised that I was Dylan Klebold laughed as well, or just questioned why I did it with a light chuckle. None of the faculty recognised me, though. One of the teachers said I was Neo from The Matrix. My math teacher wanted to see what my shirt read, which made me scared since she could recognise it from simply looking at my shirt. I showed her anyway, and she didn't recognise it... Until after the school's assembly.

Right when my friends and I were about to do our usual stupid things we'd do during recess(I'm in Australia so yes there's a recess), my math teacher called me over to have a talk with me. She questioned who I was, and I didn't know what to say, despite being called Neo from The Matrix by another teacher earlier(I forgot, okay?).

I assumed she was suspicious of who I was because of some fuckhead seventh grader who shouted "School shooter!" across the field. My memory is very faint when it comes to remembering what we spoke about, so bear with me here. I'm sure I just told her that I had the book in my black duffel bag(yes, I went the extra mile to bring a black duffel back like the duffel bags full of pipe bombs Eric and Dylan had and used it as my backpack for the day) and she told me to go fetch it. I got the book, and she said something like "So you have this book about pulling lives back together and you decide to go as the killer."

"I mean, it wouldn't hurt to go as the antagonist, right?" I thought to myself before she told me to come with her to the principal's office. I had to wait about half an hour for the principal to come out and give me a stern, but not scary, scolding about how offensive it would've been if those who had been affected by the actual attack attended our school, but of course that wouldn't have been possible because all or most of them would've reached adulthood by now.

He got the office lady to fetch me a spare school uniform to put on. I was told to take off everything that was part of my costume(besides the pants and boots), even the fingerless glove I wore on my right hand. I had to wait even more since the principal was making a call to my mother about it, and I could hear yelling of disbelief coming from the meeting room for the teachers. I immediately recognised that it was my English teacher shouting,

"WHY WOULD SHE DO THAT!? THAT'S SO INSANE, I CAN'T BELIEVE SHE WOULD DO SOMETHING LIKE THIS!" It caused me to cry like a little baby, since she's my favorite teacher. I cried and cried until it was 'safe' to come out of the office. After being comforted and lectured simultaneously by my math teacher, I went into the auditorium where I had no choice but to watch everyone else play peewee party games like pass the parcel and so on. When all that 'fun' ended, the friend who suggested to me the idea apologised to me since he believed it was his fault for suggesting the idea in the first place. I was then called up to the office again to where I saw my mother sat in one of the seats, and she had the most deadliest look on her face I had ever seen.

Since I was still in my whiny little brat state, I tried to apologise to her, only to receive a harsh "No." in return. My mother and my principal had a short chat about what I did and it ended off with my mom stating that she was gonna take me home early. And so she did. I had noticed that I got every part of my costume back besides the t-shirt.

I speculated that they threw it away. I didn't care since I didn't plan on keeping a five dollar black t-shirt with the word 'WRATH' poorly painted on in red by myself anyway.

When we arrived home and got into the house, my mother immediately started screaming whilst beating my ass, and ranted about the same things the principal and my math teacher did before sending me off to my bedroom and taking all technology from me, which was an immediate red flag that I was gonna be grounded for a long time.

A few hours went by, and I was confronted by my father, who had gotten home from work. He began to tell me that the school could get the police involved with this and that what I did was wrong. Basically, the same things the principal told me(besides the police part, which absolutely scared the shit out of me). For the rest of the day I was quite shaken up, but my mother cooled down from her little anger attack and everything went quite normally.

The next day, I was called into the office accompanied by my father. Since my principal was sick on that day, my math and English teachers took his place for it. They began throwing questions at me like, "Why did you do it?" and stuff like that, in which I answered that it was a dark joke and was for shock value. It didn't end there, thought. My math teacher told my dad that she had noticed a pattern of darkness from me.

Earlier on in the year, I drew an artwork that was meant to resemble relations to Greek mythology for art class(my math teacher is also my art teacher btw), but she thought it was demonic stuff. She also noticed that when discussing the film "Schindler's List", I was making jokes and laughing during class with a friend. I'm honestly still quite bothered about the art one because I didn't bother saying anything about how it had nothing to do with edgy demonic shit.

My English teacher stated that she was going to take the Sue Klebold book back to the library, which made me feel even more crummier since I was actually really interested in that book. My teachers and father discussed more stuff in which I didn't really pay attention to before I was taken back home for my one day suspension, which I had to spend listening to hipster podcast stuff from my father and take notes since he probably believed I liked satanic stuff. When my sister got home, she told me that everyone in our class questioned if I was okay and everything like that.
